Subject: SLA & Premium Support: pilot -> production path

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost numbers were compelling. Before we commit the pilot, procurement asked for a clearer picture of how your SLA and premium support would work as we move from pilot to production. Our team expects a fast ramp over Q1 (volume doubling month-over-month), so we need clarity on: 

- Uptime tiers and corresponding credit calculations (pilot vs production)
- Response time windows by severity (S1/S2/S3) and oncall coverage during peak weekends
- How credits are applied (invoice offset vs banked credits) and any amortization rules
- Escalation coverage: how and when would Redwood loop in engineering/hardware ops for Dedicated instances

Can you send a one-pager or term sheet we can give to finance and procurement? We likely need something that accommodates a short pilot with a softer SLA, then a hardened SLA for go-live.

Best,
Samira

Subject: Re: SLA & Premium Support: pilot -> production path

Samira — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to outline a phased approach that maps to your pilot -> production ramp. High-level proposal: 

Phase A (Pilot, 30–60 days):
- "Assurance" SLA: 99.5% uptime target, credits calculated on monthly uptime shortfall and applied as a banked credit (not immediate invoice offset)
- Response windows: S1 1 hour P1 phone triage (business hours + extended weekday oncall), S2 4 hours, S3 24 hours
- Escalation: priority routing to Tier 2 support; engineering on-call engagement with 4-hour SLA for dedicated issues

Phase B (Production, post-commit):
- Hardened SLA: 99.95% uptime for Hosted / 99.9% for Dedicated depending on config; credits escalate non-linearly if uptime drops below thresholds
- Response windows: S1 30 min phone + immediate paging, S2 2 hours, S3 8 hours; 24/7 oncall for S1
- Escalation: guaranteed engineering hot-path support and monthly operational review 

Credit mechanics (proposal): banked credits for pilot that convert to invoice offsets after go-live if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity or spend commit. Credit tiers based on minutes of downtime per month (we provided an example matrix below).

Next steps: I can send a short term sheet + example credit math. Is procurement able to accept banked credits that carry through the pilot, or do they require immediate invoice reductions? Also, would you like us to include a small, one-time onboarding retainer for 24/7 S1 coverage during the first 90 days?

—Marcus

Subject: Phased SLA term sheet (draft) + credit matrix

Hi Samira — attaching a short draft we can share with procurement and an example credit matrix. Key differences from Marcus' note: 

- We propose banked credits during pilot with a defined conversion trigger: cumulative banked credits >= $12,500 OR end of pilot converts to invoice offset on signature of a 12-month commit.
- Pilot uptime target 99.6% (slightly higher) to reflect your expected short ramp; production targets are as Marcus outlined.
- Credit calculation (example):
  - uptime >= 99.95%: 0% credit
  - 99.9%–99.95%: 5% of monthly invoice
  - 99.5%–99.9%: 15% of monthly invoice
  - <99.5%: 40% of monthly invoice + escalation credit (one-time operational remediation credit)

- For Dedicated: engineering acknowledgement SLA is 2 hours for S1 with guaranteed on-call handoff; there is a modest one-time Rx onboarding fee for hybrid/on-prem escalation enablement (covers runbook integration and VPN/KMS validation).

Attachments included as stubs: redlines-phased-sla-term-sheet.pdf, phased-credit-matrix.xlsx

If procurement wants invoice offsets instead of banked credits we can flip to an immediate offset model but that changes the economics — expect a ~3–5% uplift on price to compensate. Happy to walk procurement through both models.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Pricing, Redwood Inference

- Pilot = low-friction, banked-credit model that converts on commit OR when credits hit $12.5k. This reduces procurement's near-term accounting headache while preserving alignment on risk.
- Production = hardened SLA with stronger uptime targets and 24/7 S1 coverage; credits are higher if guaranteed uptime is missed.
- Dedicated/hybrid: one-time enablement fee to cover runbook & secure network integration; engineering acknowledgement for Dedicated S1 is 2 hours with immediate escalation to hardware ops.

Samira — let me know procurement's preference on invoice offset vs banked-credit (they'll get a clear comparison in the sheet). If you want, we can prepare a clean one-page term sheet and a marked-up legal clause for your counsel.
